title: Python and GitHub Actions style conventions: where they live now (shared skills, not path-scoped rules)
answers: Where are the Python coding and testing conventions for MLflow defined now?
Where did the GitHub Actions workflow guidelines go after the .claude/rules move?
Why does Copilot review point to .claude/skills instead of .claude/rules?
I want to change the workflow style guide for pipefail or secrets; which file do I edit?
body:
Path: The MLflow style guidance for Python source/tests and for GitHub Actions workflows and composite actions. Python conventions are in .claude/skills/python-style/SKILL.md; workflow and action conventions are in .claude/skills/github-actions-style/SKILL.md. Both are reached by agents through .agents/skills -> ../.claude/skills, and Copilot code review reads them via .github/instructions/python.instructions.md (applyTo **/*.py) and .github/instructions/github-actions.instructions.md (applyTo .github/workflows and .github/actions yml).
Rule: Edit the style content in the SKILL.md files, not in .claude/rules/ (those path-scoped files were removed). Keep the .github/instructions/*.instructions.md files as thin pointers to the skill paths, and keep their applyTo scopes unchanged.
Constraints: The skills need to be selected or invoked by an agent; this layout does not guarantee automatic activation or automatic Copilot review discovery. Skill frontmatter (name, description) is what makes the skill discoverable.
applies: Repository-level layout for MLflow's Python and GitHub Actions style guidance; applies when locating or editing these conventions.
says: Automated code reviews reference missing or outdated project style guide files.
